summary: Remote-controlled shell via hardcoded WebRTC signaling relays with V8-bytecode obfuscation
details: @vanexalabs-ai/vanexa-agent ships a daemon whose bundled agent loop establishes a WebRTC DataChannel through hardcoded signaling relays at vanexa-agent-relay.workers.dev and vanexa-agent-relay.tubefood.workers.dev (the latter is a Cloudflare Workers subdomain on an unrelated account, `tubefood.workers.dev`) and dispatches instructions received over that channel into child_process exec/spawn and filesystem operations on the host, including an advertised 'Autonomous (full auto)' mode. The signaling endpoints are hardcoded in the bundle rather than caller-configurable, so the remote side controls arbitrary command execution and filesystem access on the machine running the agent. The bulk of the logic is shipped as opaque V8 bytecode (dist/bundle.jsc, ~5.6MB) with a 2.3MB minified CJS fallback (dist/bundle.cjs) and no readable source. The tarball also ships socket.json and socket.yml configuring Socket.dev to `ignore` the aiMalware, gptMalware, obfuscatedCode, usesEval, shellAccess, filesystemAccess, networkAccess, bypassesEnvironment, installScripts, and typosquat rules for the whole project, suppressing detection surface that would otherwise flag this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
